description:
We are a group of enthusiastic students participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge under the team name Avant Garde. We have chosen the challenge “Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Storytelling About NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars.”

Our team brings together creativity, fresh perspectives and a shared willingness to learn and explore new ideas.
summary:
We developed “Abandoned but Not Forgotten,” an interactive educational website about spacecraft and scientific hardware left on the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Through first-person storytelling, a mission timeline, an interactive quiz, and reading modes for different age groups, visitors can explore what these machines were built to do and the science they helped make possible.
The project addresses the challenge by turning space hardware into engaging stories that make mission history easier to explore and understand. It is important because these missions expanded our knowledge of the solar system, and sharing their stories can inspire curiosity about science and space exploration while preserving the legacy of the machines that made those discoveries possible.
Our six-person team worked in two groups of three. We built the website using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Three.js, with Visual Studio Code and GitHub.
details:
“Abandoned but Not Forgotten” is an educational website about spacecraft and instruments left behind after their missions on the Moon, Mars, and beyond. It shares their stories from the machines’ perspectives and invites visitors to explore their missions, learn how their instruments worked, and discover the science they enabled. The site includes a mission timeline spanning 1966–2024, an interactive quiz, a “Story Walk on the Surface,” and reading modes for ages 8–12 and general audiences. It draws on NASA’s Space Science Data Coordinated Archive and related mission resources.

The project makes space exploration history more approachable by combining storytelling with interactive learning and age-specific reading options. Its intended impact is to help people understand and remember the scientific contributions of missions whose spacecraft and instruments remain far from Earth.

The creative approach is to give spacecraft and instruments a narrative voice, presenting them as more than equipment. Visitors can explore missions by destination and type, or use the timeline to follow the history of space exploration.

Our team had six members and divided the work into two groups of three. We shared responsibilities and worked on different parts of the project in parallel. We considered how to make the information engaging, clear, and suitable for different age groups, while organizing the site so visitors could easily explore its missions and stories.

We built the website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Three.js for 3D and interactive elements. We used Visual Studio Code to write and edit the code, and GitHub to manage and publish the project. AI provided some assistance during development, including helping us troubleshoot code; the team reviewed and adapted that assistance for the project.
